newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Alleged killer of Palestinian boy loses bail bid.
newsitem.headline: Alleged killer of Palestinian boy loses bail bid.

text.p: A Jewish settler suspected of beating to death an 11-year-old Palestinian boy lost a court bid on Sunday to be freed on bail.
A Jerusalem court ordered Nahum Kurman held until the end of criminal proceedings against him, saying he was suspected of "severe and cruel violence pointing to a total loss of control."
Israeli authorities on Friday charged Kurman, security chief of the Jewish settlement of Hadar Beitar, with manslaughter.
They said he kicked Hilmi Shousa to the ground, placed his foot on the boy's neck and beat him on the head with a pistol butt while on a hunt for stone-throwers a week ago in the West Bank.

Kurman, a religious Jew, faces up to 20 years in jail if convicted. He was not asked to enter a plea but his brother, Aharon told reporters outside the courtroom on Sunday: "He says the boy simply fell and hit his head on a rock."
A group of rabbis paid a condolence call to the Shousha family in the West Bank village of Husan on Sunday.
"It was a horrible thing," Yitzhak Bardea, chief rabbi of the Israeli city of Ramat Gan, near Tel Aviv, told Hilmi's father as they shook hands.

"We didn't come to make a political statement. We came as rabbis to say we are saddened at the loss of life," Rabbi Yehuda Gilad, one of four Jewish clergymen who visited the village near Bethlehem, told Israel Television.
